HAI and Antimicrobial Use Point Prevalence Survey

Data quality and survey report (synthetic data)

09 November 2026

All data in this report is synthetic. It was generated from scratch in the layout of a REDCap export for an HAI and antimicrobial use point prevalence survey: 540 patients in 10 invented hospitals, with data errors planted deliberately to demonstrate the quality checks. No real patient, facility or programme data was used. The HAI classification uses simplified definitions for demonstration (see the definitions on each page).

1. Data quality

543records exported (562 fields)
122validation rules applied
67queries raised on 67 records
27critical queries
516records included in analysis (95.0%)

Records with an open critical query (impossible value, unidentifiable or duplicated patient) are held back from the survey analysis on the following pages until the hospital resolves them. Records with major or minor queries stay in, flagged.

Rule Severity Check Queries
LOG_ward_survey_date Major Survey date differs from the date the rest of the ward was surveyed 9
DUP_patient_uniqueid Critical Same patient ID entered under more than one record 6

DAT_device_removal_before_insertion Critical A device removal date is before its insertion date 3
DAT_long_stay Minor Length of stay over 365 days 3
DAT_specimen_after_survey Critical A specimen was collected after the survey date 3

LOG_amu_no_but_agent Major Not on antimicrobials, but an agent is recorded 3
LOG_amu_yes_no_agent Major On antimicrobials, but no agent recorded 3
LOG_review_form_missing Major Patient meets HAI review criteria and a review trigger, but the classification form is blank 3
MIS_ward Critical ward is missing 3

DAT_surgery_after_survey Critical A procedure date is after the survey date 2
LOG_male_obstetric Major Male patient on an obstetrics and gynaecology ward 2

Severity. Critical: impossible or unidentifiable, so the record is held back. Major: missing or inconsistent, so it would bias an estimate. Minor: unusual but possible, so it only needs confirmation.

2. General survey report

HAI chart review criteria (set in R/03_derive_indicators.R): Non-surgical: receiving antimicrobials on the survey date and on hospital day 3 or later. Surgical: an operative procedure in the 30 days before the survey date. A patient meeting either set of criteria undergoes HAI chart review.

6. UTI

Reviewed for UTI: under HAI chart review (non-surgical criteria) with a urine culture, urinalysis, urinary catheter or clinician-documented UTI, so the UTI classification form was completed. Meets the UTI definition (simplified): positive urine culture (not Candida only) in the review window, at least one UTI sign or symptom not present on admission, and onset on hospital day 3 or later. Catheter-associated (CAUTI): urinary catheter in place for more than 2 days on the date of event.

7. BSI

Reviewed for BSI: under HAI chart review (non-surgical criteria) with a blood culture in the review window, so the BSI classification form was completed. Meets the BSI definition (simplified): blood culture positive for a recognised pathogen in the review window (a single coagulase-negative staphylococcus is treated as a contaminant), not present on admission, onset on hospital day 3 or later. Central line-associated (CLABSI): central line in place for more than 2 days on the date of event.

8. Pneumonia

Reviewed for pneumonia: under HAI chart review (non-surgical criteria) with chest imaging, a respiratory culture or clinician-documented pneumonia, so the pneumonia classification form was completed. Meets the pneumonia definition (simplified): chest imaging consistent with pneumonia in the review window, fever plus at least one respiratory sign or symptom, not present on admission, onset on hospital day 3 or later. Ventilator-associated (VAP): ventilator in place for more than 2 days on the date of event.
